title: Tie a necktie on a collar form
instruction: Tie a four-in-hand necktie on the collar form and leave it ready to wear.
context: Preparing a wearable tie requires managing a broad fabric strip, keeping its face outward and adjusting a knot to a collar and usable length.
setup: Proposed props: a child-sized 1.10 m fabric necktie with pointed ends, 70 mm wide end and 35 mm narrow end, with pale and gold opposite-edge markings (front face: pale left, gold right with wide tip down), nominal effective thickness 1.2 mm and mass 28.5 g; a rigid 110 mm diameter, 65 mm high collar/neck form centred at x=0.50,y=0,z=1.12 on the YAM station; a rigid polymer 160 x 280 x 45 mm shoulder block centred at x=0.50,y=0,z=1.065, with its top at the lower neck edge z=1.0875; two 8 x 35 x 55 mm collar points centred at x=0.441,y=+/-0.039,z=1.096; a central 25 mm square post at x=0.50,y=0 from z=0.7475 to 1.12, with a 180 x 160 x 12 mm base centred at x=0.50,y=0,z=0.7535 on the 0.7475 m table. Start with an untied, uncrossed tie draped around the collar and both ends accessible. A 3 mm dark centre mark identifies y=0 on the front of the form. Tip length is measured from its lower edge at z=1.0875 m. The exact naturally settled reset remains to be validated; the current half-wrap is only a gravity-settling diagnostic.
scoring: Proposed: 0.5 for a verified four-in-hand remaining after release for 5 seconds; 1.0 if also centred within 15 mm of the collar mark, neckband gap at most 10 mm, wide face outward without a half-twist, narrow end behind it with its tip at least 10 mm above the wide tip, and wide tip 280–320 mm below the collar edge. Otherwise 0. Damage, self-intersection, hidden attachment or artificial tightening invalidates the run. See JUDGING.md.
run_limit: Proposed: 3,600 control steps, 3 minutes at 20 Hz, including the final 5-second released hold.
reset_notes: Untie and restore the same collar drape without a crossing or preformed loop. Final measured reset is not yet available. Simulation initialization uses one raw environment reset followed by exactly 100 control steps (5 seconds at 20 Hz) holding the ordinary ready posture, allowing native cloth and free props to settle. This same procedure is required for every policy; final stable reset evidence is pending.
fidelity: Implemented native triangular surface FEM preserves width, bending, stretch and self-contact. A single effective shell approximates the sewn/interlined tie, with a rigid collar form. No round-rope substitute, prescribed knot motion or runtime attachment. Material response and functional knot retention are not validated.
scores: Not evaluated. No demo or Dream score exists.
